papers.title: Modeling of the thermal physical process and study on the reliability of linear energy density for selective laser melting
papers.abstract: A finite element model considering volume shrinkage with powder-to-dense process of powder layer in selective laser melting (SLM) is established. Comparison between models that consider and do not consider volume shrinkage or powder-to-dense process is carried out. Further, parametric analysis of laser power and scan speed is conducted and the reliability of linear energy density as a design parameter is investigated. The results show that the established model is an effective method and has better accuracy allowing for the temperature distribution, and the length and depth of molten pool. The maximum temperature is more sensitive to laser power than scan speed. The maximum heating rate and cooling rate increase with increasing scan speed at constant laser power and increase with increasing laser power at constant scan speed as well. The simulation results and experimental result reveal that linear energy density is not always reliable using as a design parameter in the SLM.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM热物理过程建模，未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡、疲劳性能或生物医学植入物相关主题。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication of porous biomedical implants, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no surface characterization or osseointegration discussion.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM中热物理过程建模及线能量密度可靠性。
summary_zh.method: 建立考虑体积收缩的有限元模型，进行激光功率与扫描速度参数分析。
summary_zh.result: 模型提高温度分布与熔池尺寸预测精度，线能量密度并非可靠参数。
summary_zh.validation: 仿真结果与实验测量对比验证准确性。

summary_en.motivation: To model the thermal physical process in selective laser melting and evaluate the reliability of linear energy density as a design parameter.
summary_en.method: A finite element model incorporating volume shrinkage and powder-to-dense transition was developed, with parametric analysis of laser power and scanning speed.
summary_en.result: The model improved accuracy in predicting temperature distribution and melt pool dimensions; linear energy density was found not always reliable.
summary_en.validation: Simulation results were compared with experimental measurements.

papers.title: A virtual model for biofabrication of vascularized bone matrix
papers.venue: Journal of Cell Science and Therapy

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种虚拟模型用于生物制造血管化骨基质，但未涉及AI或机器学习方法，与用户研究方向关联度低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage, lacks experimental validation, and does not address autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 建立血管化骨基质的生物制造虚拟模型
summary_zh.method: 基于计算建模的虚拟生物制造方法
summary_zh.result: 提出一种虚拟模型框架但缺乏实验验证

summary_en.motivation: This work aims to create a virtual model for the biofabrication of vascularized bone matrix.
summary_en.method: The study employs computational modeling to simulate the biofabrication process.
summary_en.result: A virtual model framework is proposed but lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Isolation and characterization of human nasoseptal cartilage derived stem/progenitor cells (CSPCs) for cartilage biofabrication
authors: Zita M Jessop Ayehsa AlSabah I Simoes C Thornton

corresponding_authors.name: Zita M Jessop Ayehsa AlSabah I Simoes C Thornton

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了鼻中隔软骨干细胞，但完全没有涉及人工智能，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: No AI or machine learning methods used; no integration into any bioprinting workflow stage.

summary_zh.motivation: 从鼻中隔软骨中分离干细胞用于软骨生物制造。
summary_zh.method: 通过酶消化分离细胞并表征其干细胞特性。
summary_zh.result: 成功分离出具有多向分化潜能的干细胞。
summary_zh.validation: 体外实验验证干细胞标志物和分化能力。

summary_en.motivation: To isolate and characterize stem/progenitor cells from human nasoseptal cartilage for potential use in cartilage biofabrication.
summary_en.method: Cells were isolated by enzymatic digestion and characterized for stem cell markers and multilineage differentiation capacity.
summary_en.result: Cartilage-derived stem/progenitor cells were successfully isolated and showed chondrogenic, osteogenic, and adipogenic potential.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed in vitro through flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and differentiation assays.
